item.title: Barcelona see €70 million summer signing as ‘the new Raphinha’ after impressive start
item.description: Barcelona see €70 million summer signing as ‘the new Raphinha’ after impressive start Barcelona are comparing Anthony Gordon to Raphinha because of his work rate and defensive contribution, according to Mundo Deportivo . The report states that the England international has settled quickly into Hansi Flick’s squad and has impressed not only with his numbers, but also with the way he approaches the matches. On that note, Gordon’s pressing, running and willingness to track back are considered valuable in Barcelona’s structure, where forwards must contribute without the ball. Gordon has found his place in Barcelona’s dressing room The outlet mentions that Gordon, who signed for Barcelona for €70 million past summer, has built strong relationships with the likes of Eric Garcia, Dani Olmo and Pedri, who have helped him adapt to life at the club. Garcia and Olmo speak English well and have been important points of support, while Pedri has also helped him connect with the group. Anthony Gordon has impressed everyone at Barcelona. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) His integration matters because Flick’s system depends on coordinated movement and trust. Moreover, Gordon sees Barcelona as a project where he can compete for titles, establish himself among Europe’s elite and strengthen his standing internationally. Work rate is central to the Raphinha comparison Gordon is a skilful and powerful winger who combines attacking ability with a high level of physical effort. He presses opponents, tracks back and continues running throughout matches. These qualities have drawn comparisons with Raphinha, whose commitment without possession has become a defining part of his game at Barcelona. Anthony Gordon is called ‘ a second Raphinha ‘. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) In fact, those within the club call him “a second Raphinha” thanks to his similarities with the Brazilian style, where his defensive efforts help the team maintain its intensity. Decision-making is an area to improve Despite his promising start, Gordon recognises that he still has room to develop. One of his priorities is improving his decision-making, particularly identifying when to take on an opponent and when to choose a pass or another option. For what it is worth, his experience in English football has largely been influenced by a more direct, box-to-box style, but at Barcelona, he is learning to operate within a possession-based system that requires careful reading of space and movement.

item.title: Real Madrid midfield star rediscovers his best form under Jose Mourinho
item.description: Real Madrid midfield star rediscovers his best form under Jose Mourinho Real Madrid have enjoyed an excellent resurgence under Jose Mourinho over the past couple of months. Several individual performances have been crucial for Los Blancos , but none has been more striking than Jude Bellingham’s return to his devastating best. After a couple of difficult seasons in the Spanish capital, Bellingham is back to the form that took Spanish football by storm during his debut season at the club. Having a fully fit and firing Bellingham is great news for Los Blancos, especially with Madrid aspiring to win trophies this season. Arsenal legend Thierry Henry has praised Bellingham’s form and has identified Real Madrid as title contenders this campaign. “Real Madrid put in a great performance; playing like that, they’re contenders for the Champions League. “They’re improving a lot as the weeks go by. Something’s happening at Real Madrid – watch out,” he explained. His influence on the team is now beginning to extend beyond just his ability to score goals and provide assists. Bellingham rediscovering his match-winning instincts The midweek clash against PSV Eindhoven provided the perfect demonstration of what Bellingham can add to this team. Bellingham has returned to his very best this season. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) The Englishman came on at half-time with Los Blancos struggling to impose themselves and trailing 1-0. He immediately turned the game on its head, scoring a spectacular goal that will be remembered for a long time. Bellingham has already scored seven goals this season, just one fewer than he managed throughout last season. The numbers are moving closer to the kind of attacking output he produced in his debut season in the Spanish capital. Bellingham scored 23 goals and provided 13 assists from midfield to help Los Blancos complete the La Liga and Champions League double. Mourinho has unlocked a different Bellingham Under Jose Mourinho, Bellingham has combined his attacking instincts with greater defensive discipline. He has always been an intelligent presser, but the Englishman is also taking more responsibility in possession and influencing play. The best example of this came in the Clasico that Real Madrid won back in October. With the game heading for a draw, Bellingham helped his team secure all three points. item.description: Tyson Fury (left) has 36 wins, two defeats and one draw as a professional, while Anthony Joshua has 30 wins and four defeats [Getty Images] They have conquered the world, filled stadiums and transformed British boxing. Now, after more than a decade of lingering tension and endless debate, Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are finally preparing to share a ring. They are from different worlds, with contrasting personalities and wildly different journeys to the summit of heavyweight boxing. Fury is the unpredictable showman who dethroned a seemingly unbeatable champion. Joshua is the Olympic golden boy who became a global superstar. Who is better? Who has achieved more? The arguments have raged in pubs, boxing gyms and across social media. We may soon get our answer, but whatever happens when the first bell sounds in Cardiff in the early hours of 12 December, their greatest achievement may already be secure. Together, Joshua and Fury have taken British heavyweight boxing to new heights, attracting wider audiences and inspiring the next generation. How Fury and Joshua brought big-time heavyweight boxing to Britain Britain had produced heavyweight champions before, but for years many of the division's biggest fights took place overseas. Lennox Lewis fought some of his defining bouts in Las Vegas and Memphis. Challengers travelled to Germany when the Klitschko brothers reigned. In November 2015, Fury outpointed Wladimir Klitschko in Dusseldorf. Less than five months later, Joshua knocked out Charles Martin at London's O2 Arena to win his first world title in his 16th professional fight. "Bosh, that's it. The revolution starts in that six-month period," said BBC Radio 5 Live boxing pundit Steve Bunce, who was interviewed for the BBC documentary Rivals: Fury v Joshua. Joshua's former trainer Rob McCracken saw an early sign of his appeal in Birmingham, where a show sold out with Joshua on the undercard. "I'm from Birmingham, and it's hard to get a big crowd that sort of size," McCracken says. Promoters soon realised Joshua was bringing in a different audience and could sell tickets almost instantly. By 2017, Joshua was fighting in front of 90,000 fans at Wembley Stadium, where he stopped Klitschko, while Fury's trilogy with Deontay Wilder made him a box-office draw in the USA. "The two of them have been in eight massive stadium fights over an eight-year period," Bunce says. "That's reshaping British boxing history." item.title: What makes or breaks a high press?
item.description: Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz spearhead Liverpool's press under Andoni Iraola [Getty Images] A good high press has been the basis for some of the most successful sides in modern football but a well-oiled pressing machine has many moving parts - all requiring close attention. When an out-of-possession plan is implemented poorly, entire seasons can fall apart. So, what determines whether a press works or fails? And how are the always-adapting Premier League teams exploiting high presses this season? 1. Establishing intent When a team decides to press, they must first establish their intention. This informs how the players act. Speaking to DAZN Portugal , Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler was asked about whether a good press relied more on physicality or courage. "A really good question," he began. "When you want to press high you need the courage and mindset to do it. Our mindset is we press to score, we don't just press to win the ball back." In coaching, clarity is key - particularly when it comes to creating alignment in the squad and Hurzeler is deliberate in simplifying big ideas when delivering messages to his players, a skill he practised as a radio pundit during the World Cup. "[Punditry] helps you as a coach in that you have to summarise things in a short and easy way so that everyone understands," he said. "Football might get more complex but simplicity counts." Hurzeler's "pressing to score" is a phrase that communicates many ideas in a memorable three words: intensity, being proactive, and immediate forward-thinking on winning the ball. It also frames pressing in a way that makes it easy for attackers to buy into, in the form of goals. "You want commitment from everyone on the pitch," Hurzeler explained. "If just one has doubts, the whole press is gone." The Red Bull school of coaching uses a similarly succinct phrase - "the last step" to address these ideas around intention, collectiveness and aggression. Summarised by Tactx , whose coaches have worked under the Red Bull model, the last step refers to "players [being] coached to attack through the opponent, using the final step to lunge aggressively at the ball". "This action commits the defender fully and is often the decisive moment that allows possession to be won." Pressing to engage rather than just to close distances ensures the team in possession aren't given the time or space to play through otherwise half-hearted pressure. 2. Knowing when to press and when to drop off When discussing how good or bad a team is at pressing, how much they run is often brought up. item.title: Ebnoutalib expected to stay at Frankfurt despite rumours of a winter exit
item.description: Ebnoutalib expected to stay at Frankfurt despite rumours of a winter exit It's becoming apparently clear that Younes Ebnoutalib will not be leaving Eintracht Frankfurt during the winter transfer window. Contrary to other sources, Sky Germany understands that a move for the 23-year-old in January is simply out of the question. Earlier in the week, Sport BILD reported that a quick departure was possible, with the striker said to be feeling undervalued at Frankfurt. Whether there will be any further developments regarding this player remains to be seen, but an exit in early 2027 seems off the cards. Borussia Dortmund is fully informed about all the details of a potential summer deal. A transfer fee of €35million is being discussed. On Wednesday, BVB were listed as potential suitors for Ebnoutalib, with Bayern Munich, Juventus and Tottenham Hotspur also keen .

item.description: Manchester City have a lot of bigger concerns right now but some of Enzo Maresca ’s staff have naturally been conscious of the noise around David Raya . The goalkeeper was not wearing a sling at Tuesday’s Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund, after he had so conspicuously been photographed sporting one on London’s busiest street just two days before. It’s certainly true the injury suffered at Newcastle United is nowhere near as bad as first feared, with contact on a nerve having apparently caused the initial issue. Some on the City side have wondered whether Mikel Arteta is using it to play his usual games. The manager likes to use media and even official squad photos to keep opposition guessing. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta during the Champions League clash with Dortmund (PA) It would be especially understandable here, since this position could go a long way to deciding Sunday’s game. The entire decision on Raya, in fact, draws out so many of its strands and storylines. Both sides are especially attuned to it since it was as recently as March's Carabao Cup final that Pep Guardiola ’s response to the Kepa Arrizabalaga selection essentially decided that game. It might even have been the Catalan’s last piece of genius in England. Arsenal couldn’t play out of the press without Raya's passing, and City gradually shut them down. The tactical effect of it was so pronounced that it framed the thinking of both clubs ahead of April’s suffocatingly tense Premier League showdown. That 2-1 City win might well go down as one of those influential defeats, rather than decisive victories, because of the effect on Arsenal. They actually gleaned confidence and instruction, to win all of their remaining games. Injured Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya and Newcastle United striker William Osula in discussion (Getty) And now they're champions, and intent on asserting exactly what that means - with Raya's injury currently the primary concern. item.title: 'You're always allowed to dream' - Marco Rose backs Bournemouth's Europa League ambitions after 10-man comeback against Celta Vigo seals 10th straight victory
item.description: FBL-EUR-C3-CELTA VIGO-BOURNEMOUTH - AFP Bournemouth manager Marco Rose has backed his side's Europa League ambitions after a stunning 10-man comeback against Celta Vigo sealed a club-record 10th straight victory on Thursday. Despite Bafode Diakite's early red card, the Cherries fought back to win 2-1 in Spain and maintain their perfect start to their debut European campaign. Cherries stun Celta in Spain Bournemouth overcame a first-half deficit and a red card to extend their winning streak in Spain . Iago Aspas had curled Celta ahead before Bafode Diakite was dismissed via VAR in the 23rd minute for catching Couhaib Driouech high on the ankle. Second-half goals from Alvaro Rodriguez and substitute Rayan then turned the match around as Celta saw three strikes ruled out for offside. Rose embraces European trophy dream The dramatic turnaround left Bournemouth top of the Europa League table with five wins from five, becoming only the third side to win their opening five major European fixtures after Nuremberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73. Already rated among the tournament favourites with a 26 per cent title chance by the Opta supercomputer before kick-off, Rose refused to dampen expectations. Speaking to TNT Sports , Rose said: "You're always allowed to dream. If you get into a competition like this, you want to achieve the best possible things, but we know that there's a long way to go, with many games. "Now it's about getting in the top eight, to avoid even more games for us, as a Premier League club, and then we can see, step by step. Staying humble is good in our situation, and working hard." Remarkable turnaround under German boss Thursday's triumph made Bournemouth the first Premier League team in any competition to win after trailing with 10 men at half-time since Liverpool beat Newcastle United in August 2023. Remarkably, Rose made eight changes from their previous league outing, yet his side improved after the dismissal, firing seven second-half shots compared to three before the interval. Momentum shifted when Rodriguez headed in Amine Adli's inswinging cross, before fellow substitutes Adrien Truffert and Marcus Tavernier combined to set up Rayan's winner. It caps an extraordinary revival for Andoni Iraola's successor, who sat just above the relegation zone without a league win after losing 5-1 to Chelsea on October 10, only to reel off 10 straight wins while scoring at least twice in every game. Quick turnaround awaits at Fulham Rose now faces another rapid turnaround as fifth-placed Bournemouth travel to Fulham on Sunday in the Premier League. Sitting just four points off second place, the Cherries will be eager to carry their relentless momentum back into domestic action. Securing another victory in west London would keep their remarkable winning streak alive while easing the pressure of juggling European and league commitments.

item.title: Bournemouth make history! Marco Rose's men set unprecedented English record in Europe after comeback win over Celta Vigo
item.description: Real Club Celta v AFC Bournemouth - UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Bournemouth’s fairy-tale start to life in continental competition reached new heights on Thursday night as they secured a historic victory on Spanish soil. Marco Rose’s side showed incredible resilience to overcome both a goal deficit and a first-half red card to maintain their flawless record in the Europa League. Ten-man Bournemouth stage stunning second-half turnaround Iago Aspas curled Celta Vigo ahead before Bafode Diakite saw red in the 24th minute for a poorly timed tackle, leaving the visitors a goal and a player down at half-time. Despite playing over an hour with 10 men, Bournemouth controlled the game after the interval. Amine Adli crossed early in the second half for Alvaro Rodriguez to head an equaliser, before substitute Rayan swept in the winner 12 minutes from time to seal a 2-1 victory . Adli hails character after dramatic comeback Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Adli praised his side's resilience in Spain. "We showed a lot of character," he said. "It's amazing to come back in this way and go back home with the three points." He also detailed his thinking behind the assist for the equaliser. "I was looking for someone in the box," Adli added. "I know Alvaro is very good in the air and he was in a good position so I just tried to deliver a dangerous ball towards the far post." Historic milestone extends club-record winning streak Bournemouth are now the first English club to win their opening five European games, and only the third in major continental competitions after Nurnberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73. The triumph also extends their club-record winning run to 10 matches across all competitions, complementing their fifth-place Premier League standing. Adli credited the squad's half-time belief for driving the turnaround. "I think it was down to the mentality of the players. From the moment we conceded the goal, and even after the red card, we always believed in ourselves," he noted. "What's fantastic is that in the dressing room, even before the coach started speaking, everybody was saying, 'we can do this.' Everyone was motivated and still believed we could turn things around." Knockout qualification within reach for Europa League leaders Topping the Europa League league phase table, Bournemouth have one foot in the knockout rounds. Sustaining this unshakeable mentality will be crucial as Rose's men look to safeguard both their European summit and their strong domestic position.

item.title: Man City owners should be forced to sell, say rival club chiefs
item.description: The independent commission is yet to decide on a sanction for Manchester City [Getty Images] Manchester City's owners must be forced to sell up as punishment for breaking financial rules, senior figures at Premier League clubs have told BBC Sport. This week, the chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) David Kogan claimed he has the "stomach" to take action against City, who deny wrongdoing and have appealed. The IFR has the power to remove directors of a club if they are deemed unsuitable, and even force a sale in the most serious cases. Now, executives at three top-flight rivals have told the BBC that they believe this is the appropriate punishment for City, who were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations rules between 2009 and 2018, and failing to co-operate with an investigation. Premier League clubs to cover legal costs if Man City sponsors sue Rival clubs want range of punishments for Man City The independent commission has yet to decide on a sanction that could range from a fine, to a points deduction, the stripping of past titles, or even expulsion from the league. But speaking on condition of anonymity, one executive claimed they are among a group of clubs who feel that City's punishment will be irrelevant unless the owners are also forced to sell. They added that anything less will make them question why they are funding the regulator through a levy. In comments that reveal the level of anger felt by some of City's rivals, another claimed the rule breaches had undermined the league's credibility, and that they would not be able to draw a line under the scandal and move on if the owners were allowed to stay. The club were found guilty of inflating revenues and disguising losses by £900m through "sham" commercial arrangements. Manchester City's owners are Abu Dhabi United Group - a private investment company belonging to United Arab Emirates vice-president and deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Mansour. The executive who spoke anonymously said that clubs had been asked by the Premier League to refrain from publicly revealing their views on sanctions, and let the process run its course, although some are said to have privately made their opinions clear to IFR officials. They acknowledged that some clubs were less opinionated about a punishment. Other clubs the BBC approached declined to comment, or said they were willing for the independent commission panel and IFR to reach their own conclusions following the publication of the commission's ruling in September. But the fact that some clubs want the unprecedented sanction of a forced sale will put pressure on Kogan to mete out the harshest penalty possible in what is being seen as a defining test of the watchdog just over a year after it was established. It also comes amid mounting questions over whether wider UAE trade and investment in UK projects could be impacted by such a move. item.description: ESPN and Kirk Herbstreit are set to talk about a new contract in the near future Getty ESPN and Kirk Herbstreit will reportedly talk about a new contract after the college football season Getty Kirk Herbstreit recently signed a new deal with Amazon Prime Video Getty Kirk Herbstreit has been the face of ESPN’s college football coverage for three decades. Whether that continues past this season is now a fair question. Herbstreit’s ESPN contract runs out after the current college football season. On Wednesday, Front Office Sports’ Ryan Glasspiegel reported that Herbstreit and the network were closing in on a long-term deal. However, ESPN wasn’t ready to commit to that just yet. The network quickly pushed back on the report, and its timeline for a decision is clear: it’s waiting until the season is over. ESPN Shoots Down Report on Kirk Herbstreit Contract Getty ESPN and Kirk Herbstreit will reportedly talk about a new contract after the college football season It’s not often a network publicly shuts down a report that it’s about to keep its biggest college football star. item.title: Coach Not Worried About UFC Stripping Carlos Ulberg
item.description: Carlos Ulberg UFC Getty Eugene Bareman, the head coach of UFC light heavyweight champion Carlos Ulberg at City Kickboxing, isn’t worried about Ulberg being stripped. Bareman said this week that Ulberg will not fight his teammate Navajo Stirling for the UFC light heavyweight title, even though there is a good argument that they are the top two fighters in their weight class. While some fans have suggested that Ulberg should be stripped because he won’t fight Stirling, Bareman said he’s not worried about that happening. Carlos Ulberg Won’t Be Stripped, Says Coach Speaking to the New Zealand Herald, Bareman said that he’s not concerned about Ulberg being stripped since there have been similar situations between two teammates not wanting to fight in the UFC and the champion not losing their belt. “There’s precedent for this all over the UFC (not stripping Ulberg),” Bareman said (via Bloody Elbow ). In fact, Bareman doesn’t even think the UFC matchmakers will offer the fight, since he’s made it clear that both men won’t fight each other. “No, because there has to be a fight on the table and it has to be offered. Why would they offer us a fight when we’ve said that. They’re not going to offer us a fight if we said that we’re not going to fight,” Bareman said. “It just wouldn’t come across the table because they know that, we’re just standing on our ground here.” Dana White’s Reaction Will Be Interesting The UFC is enjoying a rare off week this weekend for Thanksgiving, so reporters haven’t had the opportunity to ask UFC president Dana White what his thoughts on this situation are. While it’s not fair to put words in White’s mouth, we do know that White has said many times that he views the UFC as an opportunity to make money for yourself and help your family have a great life. For Stirling to make the most money possible, he would need to become the UFC light heavyweight champion, which won’t happen if he is unwilling to fight Ulberg, which appears to be the case, as Bareman has squashed the fight. Late in a tied fourth quarter, Kansas City faced third-and-10 from its own 9-yard line when quarterback Patrick Mahomes fired across the middle to wide receiver Rashee Rice . That sequence swung field position in Buffalo’s favor during a sloppy, rain-soaked defensive slugfest. Kansas City still had chances to steal the win, though special teams mistakes proved costly. Kicker Harrison Butker pushed a go-ahead 46-yard field goal wide right with 5:56 remaining, his eighth missed field goal of the season. After Rice’s overturned grab stalled Kansas City’s ensuing drive, Buffalo forced another three-and-out in the final seconds and tipped punter Matt Araiza’s kick, setting up Bills kicker Tyler Bass for a walk-off 57-yard field goal. item.title: The Curious Case of Everton Defender Jarrad Branthwaite
item.description: Less said about Brentford away the better. Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite, the lad from Carlisle is a hot topic at the best of times. The curious case of Jarrad Branthwaite is upon us. The positives Let’s get the positive things out of the way. Jarrad Branthwaite is a very good and classy defender, he makes Everton very much better when he plays and considerably worse when he doesn’t. Next to James Tarkowski, who unfortunately misses the game against Liverpool due to suspension , he has shown that he has all the attributes to be one of the best English defenders for years to come. He is quick, loves a tackle and has the brains of a defender a lot more his senior. It is a testament to the young lad that he has been linked with moves away from the club, for bigger and maybe better. Tyrique George On Joining Everton, David Moyes, and Thierno Barry Everton winger Tyrique George has been discussing joining Everton on loan and permanently, manager David Moyes, and Thierno Barry's dancing. The negatives The negative part of Jarrad Branthwaite, is that it seems he is made of biscuits. Jarrad has had a terrible time with injuries, namely his hamstring. Jarrad missed big chunks of the season last year due to this reoccurring injury. To David Moyes’ credit, he has managed the injuries of Jarrad very well, and has taken him off, left him out when he was ‘half fit’ much unlike the managers before him, who would just play him. Big clubs will be put off by this, as it seems he can’t get a full season under his belt, and maybe that is the factor of how Everton have kept him for so long. Also, the fact of how Everton play their game might put off the suitors. Everton defend deep, that is a well-known fact, so positioning is key for Branthwaite’s game. Better footballing teams will play further up the pitch, would this suit Branthwaite as the ball over the top has been known to kill Everton. Look at Harry Maguire at Leicester, then on to Man United, it shows even the best defenders struggle with the high line. Everton Have Centre-Back Decision To Make: It's Simple Everton manager David Moyes has a decision to make as to who he plays at right-back and centre-back against Liverpool due to James Tarkowski's suspension. The difficulties One thing that needs to come to an end, playing Branthwaite at left back. For someone with Jarrad’s brain, he does get sucked in and out of the left back position and seems to drift over more central. This is not necessarily Jarrad’s fault, he is just being told where to play. You can see the whole crowd, also, grimace every time he goes down off a challenge, whether it be for two seconds or two minutes minutes. We always think the worst. Hopefully, the injuries become less frequent and he can lead the back for many years to come. With success though, we will see the vultures circling for the Carlisle lad. One thing is for sure, Everton need Jarrad fit and firing come Sunday vs Liverpool. Here is hoping!

item.title: Mourinho considering bold Real Madrid midfield experiment after stunning PSV comeback
item.description: Mourinho considering bold Real Madrid midfield experiment after stunning PSV comeback Real Madrid played one of their worst halves of football in recent weeks during their 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League. Los Blancos could not get going in the first half, with the Dutch side looking far superior. However, Jose Mourinho’s half-time changes and tactical tweaks saw Real Madrid score five unanswered goals against PSV. The Portuguese manager is now considering making one of those adjustments a more regular feature of his system. According to MARCA (h/t Madrid Zone ), Mourinho has not ruled out using Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva together in a double pivot. Mourinho considering Guler-Bernardo midfield partnership Jude Bellingham changed the game for Real Madrid against PSV Eindhoven. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The experiment worked wonders against the Eredivisie side after Mourinho introduced Jude Bellingham in place of Aurelien Tchouameni at half-time. This saw Guler drop back to form a double pivot alongside Bernardo, and the trio worked very well together. The transformation was remarkable, with both Bellingham and Guler getting into advanced positions and offering plenty in terms of creativity and goalscoring. After the game, Mourinho highlighted the midfield adjustment as one of the main reasons for the second-half turnaround. While neither Guler nor Bernardo is a natural defensive midfielder, they offered Real Madrid much better control of the ball. Could the experiment become a regular feature? With Federico Valverde now permanently playing at right-back, Madrid have four options for defensive midfield. Tchouameni and Bernardo have proven to be the preferred pairing, with Eduardo Camavinga and Arda Guler providing alternatives. Arda Guler offers a different level of creativity from deep-lying midfield. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) The former is the only naturally defensive option in that position, but there are games when Los Blancos need more on the ball than his ball-winning prowess. Deploying Guler deep gives Real Madrid a Toni Kroos-like playmaker in deeper areas, with the Turkish international’s vision among the best in the squad. While pairing him with Bernardo carries some obvious risks, especially in transition, it could prove to be a potent weapon when used correctly. The PSV Eindhoven game was yet another example of Mourinho’s in-game management and ability to take control of a situation. It remains to be seen whether the Bernardo-Guler experiment was a one-off or something the manager considers using in future games.

item.title: From bible study groups to Ballers in God: The rise and rise of Christianity in modern football
item.description: Christianity in football GFX - GOAL A growing number of high-profile footballers are both joining the religion and making overt demonstrations of their faith on the pitch and online, but is there something more sinister behind the movement? "I want to thank my Lord and Saviour, Jesus Christ." That phrase, or some variation of it, has often become the first thing to come out of a player's mouth in a post-match interview of late. We had become accustomed to Christian footballers subtly showing their faith by crossing themselves or pointing towards the heavens in celebration in the modern era, but now we are increasingly seeing much more overt demonstrations of Christianity, in the Premier League and beyond. While the movement might seem harmless on the face of it, as a community forms among previously disconnected Christian players on and off the pitch, we have also seen this wave of evangelism cause friction and land certain individuals in hot water amid ambiguity over the views that they hold. But what is behind the seemingly unstoppable rise of the religion in football? Growing trend We are seeing many more players make overt displays of their Christianity on the pitch and online than ever before "First of all, I want to thank Jesus Christ, my Lord and Saviour," Manchester City's Rico Lewis said in his post-match interview with TNT Sports after the Champions League victory over AEK Athens in October. "Can't even fathom doing anything without him, so all the glory and honour goes to him." That was just one example of the kind of evangelical Christianity that has become prevalent in the English game in recent years. Lewis is among a growing cohort of English and Premier League-based players who are increasingly vocal about their faith. Alongside Jeremy Doku and a clutch of other City players, he participates in weekly bible study online, according to The Athletic . Marc Guehi is another team-mate who has been open about his beliefs, the son of a former church minister. Meanwhile, at Arsenal, a group of Christian evangelical players that includes England internationals Bukayo Saka, Eberechi Eze, Noni Madueke and many others has been dubbed the 'Bible Brothers', also gathering on a regular basis to discuss passages of scripture. There is a laundry list of reasons why other teams would not sign the man who just aired quite a bit of dirty laundry . And yet: NFL teams have operated off far less logical desperation before. Rodgers’ arm strength has not fully dissipated, nor has his line-of-scrimmage command lost its argument among the best in the game. So multiple sources weren’t ready to fully rule out a Rodgers return to the NFL this season. item.description: Jamal Musiala came off the bench with 14 minutes remaining in Bayern's defeat by Lille on Wednesday [Getty Images] Bayern Munich - and representatives of one of their most prominent players -have collided over recent weeks. During the summer, the public became aware that their star 23-year-old midfielder Jamal Musiala suffered from absence seizures. This neurological condition causes a brief, sudden lapse in awareness and responsiveness. Musiala had two of these lapses during pre-season games, but episodes already happened during the previous year. At first, the shock among fans and observers was huge. Bayern kept Musiala's condition a secret for some time, and only a few insiders knew about it. In the days after Musiala's lapse during a friendly against Heidenheim, speculations arose over whether the player's medical issue had been known before he signed a highly lucrative contract extension in February 2025. But it has been confirmed by sources close to the team - and Bayern themselves - that the condition had not been detected before April 2025. One source described Musiala, at the time of signing his new contract, as being "in great health". In April 2025, days after suffering a muscle tear, Musiala caused a high-speed car crash which cost him his driver's licence. Munich's public prosecutor's office responded to a recent enquiry saying there is no evidence that the accident was caused by a lapse, nor that it was the cause of Musiala's condition. Nevertheless, checks a couple of days after the crash revealed he was suffering from absence seizures. Musiala's camp consulted numerous experts and hired doctors to treat the player, with the knowledge of Jochen Hahne, Bayern's team doctor. How close the consultations between the external doctors and Bayern's medical staff are remains a point of discussion, among many other things in this complex matter. Soon after, Musiala's football-related injuries became an issue. He broke his fibula and injured his ankle during the Fifa Club World Cup after colliding with then PSG goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma. He needed months to recover and suffered a subsequent ankle injury, likely related to the leg injury. After the 2026 World Cup he had a metal plate removed from his left foot, which affected his pre-season preparation. Musiala just recently recovered from a weeks-long absence due to a hamstring tear. On top of that, new incidents related to his neurological condition have come to light. Days before his recent return to training Musiala had another lapse, just like he did on the morning of a Champions League game against Real Madrid in April. All of this is the tragic story of a highly talented footballer who might never return to his previous level and must deal with a medical condition for the rest of his life. item.title: ‘Done & Dumb!’ Cowboys Lose In Historic Fashion To Eagles On Thanksgiving
item.description: Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott, left, and head coach Brian Schottenheimer are pictured in a file graphic. | Image by ClutchPoints The Dallas Cowboys are done … Because the Dallas Cowboys are dumb. The semi-tanking Philadelphia Eagles – playing backyard football with little real motivation – somehow erased a 21-point deficit on Thursday to mount the largest Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history, beating the heavily favored Cowboys 39-38 . Dallas’ loss dropped the Cowboys to 5-7, bringing on the reality of their slim-to-none playoff hopes. They have mastered the art of failing to win back-to-back games , and there has been another season-long constant under pack-your-bags head coach Brian Schottenheimer: This is the dumbest football team I’ve ever seen. Once again, reasons for me to testify to that same thing I’ve said in the last couple of weeks (which has caused an army of Cowboys-lovin’ fans to come hard at me) are everywhere. Want just one crunch-time mini-bundle? Multiple times in the final seconds, Eagles QB Joe Milton – the Cowboys’ third-string practice-squad reject, if you will, who made Dallas look foolish for letting him go to Philly this season – was simply trying to throw the ball out of bounds to eat clock … and not even move closer for the eventual game-winning field goal. Let me repeat: Philly, down by 2, had no designs on bothering to risk moving closer for the kick. And yet multiple times, Cowboys defenders interfered with the intended receivers … even though the intended receivers weren’t even intending to receive! Dak Prescott put up fat numbers. CeeDee Lamb put up fat numbers. Javonte Williams put up fat numbers. Quinnen Williams put up fat numbers. And they all add up to nothing. Said Prescott: “Pretty stunning. … (Numb) is a good description of how I’m feeling right now.” A team that has vehemently objected to the word “embarrassing” will now have that very word etched on its NFL gravestone. A coach who pretended to believe he is “elite” is now obviously over his head and inept. (“I would not anticipate coaching changes in the near future.”) And a promising season – promising because the NFC East has never and will never be easier to win – is done. The Cowboys are done … because the Cowboys are dumb.

item.title: Kenny Smith Pays Backhanded Compliment To LeBron James When Explaining His Longevity
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Philadelphia 76ers superstar LeBron James ‘ longevity is quite remarkable, and he made history yet again on Wednesday. James broke his own record for the oldest player to record a triple-double in the 76ers’ 111-104 win over the Miami Heat at Xfinity Mobile Arena. It shouldn’t be possible for a 41-year-old to play this well, and Kenny Smith thinks the rules are helping James. Smith explained the 22-time All-Star’s longevity on Inside the NBA on Wednesday. “We can’t forget, without Luka [Doncic] in the playoffs, he dominated the first round of the series,” Smith said. “And he still has that ability because the way the game is played today, obviously, with the lack of hand-checking, it is a parallel game. And so what happens is if you’re like a track star, and he can just stay in track shape, and he’s pushing the ball like a track star and not getting touched, not getting slowed down. “And he’s still 6’9″, 240 lbs, and can still move on a track pace,” Smith added. “And the NBA is still in danger with him on the floor.” The NBA banned hand-checking in 2004, and Smith believes James wouldn’t be as effective at his age were it still allowed. The 61-year-old thinks his athleticism and size are enough to succeed in today’s league, which is quite the backhanded compliment. Yes, James being a very good athlete helps, but he is still very skilled, and his mind remains sharp. It’s the combination of all three that still enables him to dominate games. James shone for the Los Angeles Lakers in Luka Doncic’s absence in the first round of the 2026 NBA playoffs against the Houston Rockets . The Lakers had been written off going into the series, but he led them to victory in six games. We saw that version of James again against the Heat, as he had 25 points (9-15 FG), 10 rebounds, 12 assists, and one steal. He scored 14 points in a row for the 76ers at one point in the second quarter, and we’re so blessed to still see him in action. James doesn’t always have to take over with all the talent around him, but made it clear he can dust off the cape when need be . The 76ers improved to 15-4 with this win over the Heat and remain atop the standings in the Eastern Conference. They are definitely a serious title contender, and James has his eyes set on winning his fifth championship. While some believe this would help his GOAT case, others don’t. Smith likely falls in the second category. He has made it clear that Michael Jordan is his GOAT . Smith has also said James is touching the Magic Johnson-Larry Bird “fiber,” not the Jordan “fiber.” He believes defense is what separates his former UNC teammate from LeBron. James isn’t going to get any better defensively at his age, of course. He’ll continue to be a big threat on offense, though, and he’ll be in action next when the 76ers take on the Indiana Pacers at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Friday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

item.title: Falcons’ James Pearce Jr. Could Face NFL Punishment Amid Latest Controversy
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 14: James Pearce Jr. #27 of the Atlanta Falcons warms up prior to an NFL preseason game against the Denver Broncos at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) Getty Atlanta Falcons pass rusher James Pearce Jr. has been back with the team for several weeks following his eight-game suspension, but he has yet to address local reporters since returning. Pearce was again a topic of discussion when Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski met with reporters Wednesday after social media posts from Pearce’s ex-girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson, raised questions about whether the pass rusher has attempted to contact her. While it’s unclear whether Pearce has done so, his continued refusal to speak with reporters could bring about a separate issue with the NFL. Falcons’ James Pearce Jr. Could Face NFL Fine According to 92.9 The Game’s Joe Patrick, reporters have repeatedly requested to speak with Pearce since the Falcons’ trip to Spain to face the Cincinnati Bengals earlier this month. “For more context: James Pearce Jr. has been requested by a media member to speak at every availability since the team returned from Madrid. He’s rejected every opportunity so far. From what I can tell, he last addressed local media in a scrum a year ago yesterday – Nov. 24, 2025,” Patrick wrote Wednesday on X. Patrick went on to explain why Pearce might not be able to continue turning down those requests without facing some sort of financial punishment. “He’s free to decline to speak in any particular instance, but given that every NFL player has the same (collectively bargained) clause in their contract that ‘Player will cooperate with the news media, and will participate upon request in reasonable activities to promote the Club and the League,’ he will eventually be warned and then fined if it continues.” The NFL’s 2026 media access policy requires players to be available for interviews after games and regularly throughout the practice week. It also explicitly prohibits players from boycotting the media. There is precedent for the NFL handing down substantial fines for repeated violations of its media policy. Former Seattle Seahawks running back Marshawn Lynch was hit with a combined $100,000 in fines in November 2014 for violations dating back to the previous season. Patrick did not report that Pearce has received a formal warning or been fined by the NFL. item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
